text:
alex: Quick one — I pushed a terraform change that adds an annotation to the serviceAccount in tenant-42 namespace and now external-secrets + cert-manager keep failing to fetch creds. Anyone seen an IRSA-related hiccup like this?

sara: can you paste the TF snippet or SA yaml? quick look might show an obvious annotation mismatch :eyes:

alex: here is the SA portion from the TF module we changed:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: myapp-sa
  namespace: tenant-42
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-external-secrets-tenant-42
```

infra-bot: controller/external-secrets myapp-controller[0]  ERROR: failed to assume role for serviceAccount tenant-42/myapp-sa: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::111122223333:... is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource: arn:aws:iam::999988887777:role/redwood-external-secrets-tenant-42

kevin: that log screams account mismatch. SA annotation points to account 111122223333 but the actual role arn in AWS is in 999988887777. check the TF var for account id, we recently rolled a change that templated account_id vs aws_account_id in two modules.

sara: other things to check: OIDC provider must match cluster's provider and role trust policy needs the right `sub` or `aud` condition. but first verify the role arn is correct.

 tanya: run `kubectl -n tenant-42 get sa myapp-sa -o yaml` and `aws iam get-role --role-name redwood-external-secrets-tenant-42` to confirm which account/role exists. also check `aws sts get-caller-identity` from the controller's node if debugging from a pod.

alex: yep — we accidentally used the shared-account var in the TF module for the annotation instead of the tenant account var. TF rendered the wrong arn. the role actually lives in 999988887777.

kevin: if you need a quick patch, update the annotation in the k8s manifest (kubectl -n tenant-42 patch sa myapp-sa -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn":"arn:aws:iam::999988887777:role/redwood-external-secrets-tenant-42"}}}') then reconcile the TF module fix. that should let the controller assume the role immediately.

alex: patched manually and restarted external-secrets controller pod in tenant-42, logs immediately show successful AssumeRole. rolling the TF fix now and will run `terraform plan` to ensure var scoping is cleaned. :thumbsup:

sara: nice, please add a small unit test or TF var validation so the wrong account id doesn't slip through again (maybe a pre-commit check that account ids match expected patterns).

alex: will do. thanks all — closing this after I push the TF fix.

kevin: one more FYI: if you ever see `AccessDenied` but the arn matches, double-check the role trust policy includes `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` and the issuer ARN for the OIDC provider. had a weird case where provider was recreated and thumbprint changed.

alex: noted. thanks for the tip, closing thread. :white_check_mark:
